recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Biology for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: M.C. Michael

topics.topic: Respiratory Mechanisms in Lower and Higher Organisms
subtopics: Respiratory surfaces and their characteristics (large surface area, thin, moist, vascularized)
Respiration in Amoeba (body surface), Earthworm (moist skin), Insect (tracheal system), Fish (gills)
Human pulmonary mechanism: diaphragm and intercostal muscle kinetics, inhalation vs exhalation
objectives: State four characteristics of an efficient respiratory surface
Dissect a fresh tilapia fish head to display and label gill rakers, gill arch, and gill filaments
Explain the counter-current gas exchange mechanism across fish gills

topics.topic: Excretory Systems Across Animal Phyla: Invertebrates to Mammals
subtopics: Excretory structures: contractile vacuole (Protozoa), flame cells (Flatworms), Malpighian tubules (Insects)
Structure of the mammalian kidney and microscopic nephron anatomy
Urine formation: ultrafiltration in Bowman's capsule, selective reabsorption, and tubular secretion
objectives: Map animal phyla to their specific statutory excretory organs
Draw and label the functional unit of the kidney (nephron) satisfying WAEC specifications
Explain hormonal regulation of water balance by Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)

topics.topic: Skeletal Systems: Supporting Tissues, Types of Skeletons & Human Bones
subtopics: Types of skeletons: hydrostatic (earthworm), exoskeleton (arthropods), endoskeleton (vertebrates)
Axial skeleton: skull, vertebral column (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, caudal vertebrae)
Appendicular skeleton: pectoral and pelvic girdles, bones of the forelimbs and hindlimbs
objectives: Compare biological advantages of exoskeletons and endoskeletons
Identify and draw thoracic, lumbar, and cervical vertebrae with neural spine, canal, and centrum
Classify human joints into fibrous, cartilaginous, and synovial (ball-and-socket, hinge)

topics.topic: Supporting Tissues and Movement in Plants
subtopics: Plant supporting tissues: collenchyma, sclerenchyma, xylem vessels, phloem fibers
Turgor pressure in herbaceous plant support and wilting mechanics
Secondary thickening in woody dicot stems and cambium activity
objectives: Examine transverse sections of dicot and monocot stems under a light microscope
Distinguish collenchyma from sclerenchyma based on cell wall thickening and lignification

topics.topic: Ecological Concepts: Nigerian Biomes and Environmental Factors
subtopics: Biomes of Nigeria: Mangrove Swamp, Tropical Rainforest, Southern Guinea Savanna, Northern Guinea Savanna, Sudan/Sahel
Abiotic ecological factors: temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, light intensity, soil pH, wind
Instruments for measuring abiotic factors: rain gauge, hygrometer, anemometer, Secchi disc
objectives: Characterize dominant vegetation and climatic parameters of Nigerian ecological zones
Demonstrate use of wind vane and rain gauge on the school meteorological plot

topics.topic: Population Ecology: Sampling Methods, Density and Dispersal
subtopics: Population characteristics: size, density, birth rate (natality), death rate (mortality), immigration/emigration
Ecological sampling techniques: throw-quadrat method for plants, capture-recapture technique for animals
Calculation of population density: Density = Total number of individuals / Total area sampled
objectives: Conduct a field study on school sports field calculating density of weeds using a 1m² quadrat
Apply the Lincoln-Petersen index formula to estimate grasshopper population

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Practical Laboratory Test
subtopics: Assessment on respiration, excretion, skeletons, Nigerian biomes, and population quadrat sampling
Alternative to practical specimen identification test
objectives: Demonstrate mastery of WAEC alternative-to-practical biological protocols

topics.topic: Nutrient Cycling in Nature: Carbon, Nitrogen and Water Cycles
subtopics: The Nitrogen Cycle: nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium, lightning), nitrification (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter), denitrification
The Carbon Cycle: photosynthesis, respiration, combustion of fossil fuels, decomposition
The Water Cycle and ecological balance in tropical ecosystems
objectives: Draw clear schematic flowcharts of the nitrogen cycle showing biological and chemical transformations
Identify root nodules on freshly uprooted groundnut or cowpea plants
Explain how deforestation and excessive fossil fuel burning cause global warming

topics.topic: Plant Reproduction: Floral Anatomy, Pollination and Double Fertilization
subtopics: Structure of a typical flower (calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium)
Adaptations for wind pollination vs insect pollination (Pride of Barbados, Hibiscus, Maize)
Pollen tube growth, double fertilization in angiosperms, seed and fruit development
objectives: Dissect, draw, and label floral parts of Hibiscus rosa-sinensis and Pride of Barbados
Tabulate 5 distinct morphological differences between insect and wind-pollinated flowers
Explain double fertilization: formation of 2n zygote and 3n triploid endosperm

topics.topic: Animal Reproduction: Mammalian Gametogenesis and Fertilization
subtopics: Structure of male and female reproductive systems in mammals
Spermatogenesis and Oogenesis: meiotic division stages
The human menstrual cycle: hormonal regulation by FSH, LH, Estrogen, and Progesterone
Fertilization in fallopian tube, implantation, and placenta functions
objectives: Diagram human sperm cell and ovum with appropriate biological labels
Graph hormonal fluctuations across the 28-day human menstrual cycle
State four barrier and endocrine functions of the mammalian placenta

topics.topic: Fruits and Seed Dispersal: Morphological Adaptations
subtopics: Classification of fruits: simple, aggregate, composite; dry dehiscent vs dry indehiscent vs fleshy fruits (berry, drupe)
Agents of seed/fruit dispersal: wind, water, animals, explosive mechanism
Morphological adaptations: parachute pappus (Tridax), hooks (Desmodium), buoyant fibrous mesocarp (Coconut)
objectives: Classify locally collected Nigerian fruits into drupes (mango, oil palm) and berries (tomato, orange)
Relate structural seed modifications to their agents of dispersal

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & WASSCE Practical Masterclass
subtopics: Practical dissection of flowers, bone identification, and ecological problem solving
Full review of SSS 2 Term 1 syllabus
objectives: Complete SSS 2 Biology Term 1 examination preparation

subtopics: First Term Senior Secondary 2 Examination and script moderation
objectives: Complete SSS 2 Biology Term 1 evaluation
